label: Thomas Aquinas, In octo libros Physicorum…: Denying a first mover turns the moved-mover series…
locator: VII, lect. 2 n. 892: an infinite series of movers and moved is involved
interpretation: If it is not granted that there is a first cause of the motion, then, since whatever is moved is moved by another, an infinite series of movers and moved follows (A moved by B, B by C, and so on). Read as the same proposition as Aristotle's claim ARIST-PHYS-242A16-NO-FIRST-INFINITE-CHAIN-A. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
